title: Standard deviation
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:20Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point teaches standard deviation as a measure of typical distance from the mean for Year 10 students: the closest ones use it only for normal-distribution probabilities, the empirical rule, or as one of three spread measures, which is too broad or at a different depth.

draft.title: Standard deviation
card: Standard deviation (SD) measures how far values typically sit from the mean. It is a single number that describes the spread of a data set.
A small SD means the values are bunched close to the mean. A large SD means they are spread out. An SD of 0 means every value is the same.
SD has the same units as the data. If the data is in minutes, the SD is in minutes.
Example: Set A is 4, 5, 6 and Set B is 1, 5, 9. Both have a mean of 5. Set B is further from 5, so it has the larger SD.
draft.remember: SD tells you how spread out the data is around the mean. Larger SD, more spread.

a.q: Two data sets have the same mean. Set P has an SD of 2 and Set Q has an SD of 7. What does this show?
opts: Set Q is more spread out than Set P
Set P is more spread out than Set Q
Set Q has a larger mean than Set P
Set P has more values than Set Q
a.why: A larger SD means values sit further from the mean, so Set Q is more spread out. The means are the same, so SD cannot tell you which mean is larger.
a.clue: Larger SD means values sit further from the mean.

b.q: Mia times 5 runners from two clubs over 100 m. Both clubs average 14 seconds. Club X has an SD of 0.3 seconds and Club Y has an SD of 1.2 seconds. Which is true?
opts: Club X's times are more consistent
Club Y's times are more consistent
Club X's runners are faster on average
Club Y's runners are faster on average
b.why: Club X has the smaller SD, so its times sit closer to the mean of 14 seconds and are more consistent. The means are equal, so neither club is faster on average.
b.clue: Both means are 14, so compare only the spread.

a.best: Set Q is more spread out than Set P

b.best: Club X's times are more consistent
